verification_report.summary: The complete proof, including the input Gauduchon subproof, is correct under its stated parallel-Lee convention for Vaisman. All signs, constants, integrations and equality cases were checked independently, without using the target theorem as a premise. With the complex orientation, d^c f=Jλ/(4π) and d^c(ω^(n−1))=((n−1)(n−1)!/(4π))*λ; hence Gauduchon gives δλ=0 for n≥2, and closedness gives harmonicity. For g̃=e^(−f)g, the conformal Ricci formula has Hessian-trace term +(Δf/2)g, which vanishes. The determinant formula gives ρ_g̃=n i∂∂̄f=(n/2)d(Jλ), and the Kähler conversion is Ric_g̃(U,V)=ρ_g̃(U,JV). The conformal connection and antisymmetrization produce exactly the displayed real Ricci tensor, including coefficients n, −(n−1), −1/2, 1/2 and n/2. Compactness and div A=0 give ∫S(A,A)=0. Contracted Bianchi yields ∫⟨Ric,S⟩=−(1/2)∫A(Scal)=0. Bochner has the stated positive Ricci sign; its quartic terms cancel, leaving Ric(A,A)=(1−n/2)S(A,A)+(n/2)S(B,B). Subtracting the two integral identities and dividing by n gives ∫(|S⁺|²−|S|²)=−∫|S−S⁺|²=0. Smoothness therefore forces S=S⁺ everywhere. Then S(B,B)=S(A,A), and Bochner forces ∫|S|²=0, hence ∇λ=0 everywhere. Dimension two and zeros of λ cause no exception. No bounded mass property is used; connectedness is redundant for parallelism. The attribution agrees with [Barbaro–Otiman, Section 4, Theorem A](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.18364v2#S4), checked through the official text and local archive after the required theorem-search service failed. The source uses strict LCK terminology, excluding exact Lee forms: under that convention the conclusion is Kähler when λ=0 and Vaisman otherwise. This terminology distinction does not affect the proved parallelism. Full sequential deductions are recorded in [the detailed audit](/Users/mingchen/Non-Kahler/research/rethlas/verification/results/lck_chern_ricci_rigidity_01/verification_report.md).
